title: Where zaproxy history begins
description: The earliest commits in the zaproxy repository, and traces of its Subversion past in later commit messages.

chapters.title: The first commits
chapters.text: The earliest commit in the repository is "Initial directory structure." dated 2010-08-16. The commit "Version 1.0.0" follows on 2010-09-04.

evidence.label: ZAP history page (lists 2009-2010 entries; still being written)

chapters.title: Subversion-era messages
chapters.text: Commit messages from 2011 and 2012 still mention svn, for example "Exclude svn data when copying files" (2011-03-02) and "merged changes on trunk into websockets branch fixed svn:ignore to ignore only eclipse files" (2012-05-12). This shows the project used Subversion at the time; these commits do not say where it was hosted.

chapters.title: Ten years on, in Simon Bennetts' words
chapters.text: On ZAP's tenth birthday the post "ZAP is Ten Years Old" (2020-09-06) says that on 2010-09-06 Simon Bennetts posted the first ZAP announcement, for version 1.0.0, to Bugtraq, two days after the "Version 1.0.0" commit. He describes how it began: "I started hacking on the Paros code to help me learn more about web security." (the early commits are under org/parosproxy). He wanted a community project to join and found none: "I ended up releasing ZAP in an attempt to create the community project that I wanted to join." The post lists what ZAP had done early (websockets, launching browsers, browser automation for crawling, an add-on marketplace, Zest scripting and the Heads Up Display), credits contributors and the students from Google Summer of Code and Mozilla Winter of Security, and says ZAP 2.10.0 "is going to be released fairly soon".
